_meta.note: Industry, peers, street, ownership, stock, moat, critiques, gaps and conflicts for the Piramal Pharma initiation. Sources dated on or before 30-Sep-2026.

cdmo.item: Global CDMO market ~US$250 bn, growing 7-8% a year (industry estimates in AR FY26 MD&A). US biotech funding rose 30% in FY26 and 75% YoY in H2FY26 (company, industry sources), and 'over 100%' in H1CY26 vs H1CY25 (Q1FY27 presentation). Customers want regulator-grade, multi-site supply outside China; US sites are exempt from US pharma tariffs and UK sites get a nil rate under the UK-US deal, while India's innovation-related work depends on customer negotiations (Chairperson, Q4FY26 call). Competitors have added capacity since the Covid boom and pricing is competitive (CEO, Q4FY26 call).
cdmo.src: AR FY26 MD&A; Q4FY26 call (29-Apr-2026); Q1FY27 presentation (29-Jul-2026)

adc.item: Antibody-drug conjugates are among the fastest-growing CDMO niches; Piramal's Grangemouth (UK) site was the world's first USFDA-approved commercial ADC CDMO site; ADC revenue ~US$64 mn in FY26, conjugation is the anchor service (CEO).

inhalationAnaesthesia.item: Global inhalation-anaesthesia market ~US$1 bn; sevoflurane ~84% of it; sevoflurane, isoflurane and desflurane ~81% of the IA market; high entry barriers (dedicated API and drug-product plants, vaporisers, hospital/GPO relationships). Piramal is #1 in US sevoflurane (48% value share, IQVIA) but ex-US markets face Chinese price competition; Piramal answers with lower-cost supply from Digwal.
inhalationAnaesthesia.src: AR FY26 MD&A; Q1FY27 presentation; Q4FY26 call

otc.item: Indian OTC market ~US$9 bn, growing ~8% a year to over US$11 bn by 2029 (AR FY26 MD&A); quick commerce is ~50% of Piramal's e-commerce sales; Piramal's consumer business grew about twice its markets in FY26 (Chairperson).

westAsia.item: The Middle East conflict in 2026 raised sourcing, utility, freight and insurance costs and may force extra inventory; pass-through depends on contracts (CFO, Q4FY26 call).

excluded.BIOCON: One-off and boom-bust EPS; P/E above 100x inside the window (PLAYBOOK 7c)

peers.notes: Pharma peer set set on 23-Nov-2026 (PLAYBOOK 7c). Piramal Pharma is outside the nine-name set, so all nine count. Its own window starts on 1-May-2023 (post-listing months skipped), so the factor is the nine peers' move over the same window: +5.1% EV/EBITDA (+9.5% P/E), reproduced with tools/authoring/sector-factor.js --from 2023-05-01 --metric ev. CDMO and hospital-generics names (Syngene, Sai Life, Gland, Anthem, Laurus, Divi's, Neuland) are shown for context only.

'Entering next growth orbit': broad-based 15-19% growth, margin +308bp

street.methodNote: Of the brokers that disclose a method in their latest note, two use a sum of the parts (Motilal Oswal: all three businesses on EV/EBITDA; ICICI Direct: CDMO and CHG on EV/EBITDA, PCH on EV/sales, the AbbVie JV on P/E) and two a single consolidated EV/EBITDA (Choice 24x FY28E; InCred 24.6x FY27F, a year old). JM Financial's last disclosed method (Sep-2025) was also a sum of the parts. Majority: sum of the parts built on EV/EBITDA. Nobody uses P/E: earnings are near zero.

moat.evidence: 415 inspections incl. 49 by the USFDA since FY12 with no OAI; 209 customer audits in FY26; a rare record among Indian CDMOs and a real selling point for big-pharma work.

#1 in US sevoflurane (48%) with its own API in Bethlehem and KSM in Dahej; #1 in US intrathecal baclofen; Kenalog has limited competition. CHG earns ~20% EBITDA margins (GAM estimate) with stable cash.

Integrated East-West network (13 of the top-20 customers use two or more sites), ADC conjugation at Grangemouth, HPAPI at Riverview, sterile fill-finish at Lexington; but 53% of CDMO revenue is 'other' (generic/off-patent) commercial work and on-patent manufacturing was only US$96 mn in FY26.
Overseas sites are sub-scale: CDMO EBITDA margin is high single digits vs 25-40% at Divi's, Sai Life or Anthem; ROCE 3% in FY26 on Rs8,700 cr of fixed assets.
~500 customers, top-10 36% of CDMO revenue, but one on-patent product's destocking cut FY26 CDMO revenue 10% and swung the group to a loss.
Little's, Lacto Calamine, i-pill and Saridon grow 20%+ with e-commerce at 27-28% of sales, but margins are low single digits after ~12% of sales spent on advertising.
Net debt Rs4,140 cr, 3.6x company EBITDA (4.3x on CARE's basis), above CARE's 3.5x downgrade trigger; more capex and Kenalog payments ahead.

critiques: The street's 23x CDMO multiple (MOSL) is a premium for a business earning high single-digit margins; it prices in the FY30 margin goal well before it shows up.
Order book has not yet strengthened to match better biotech funding; CDMO may grow only high single digits until RFPs convert.
Earnings quality: half of FY26 other income was forex and write-backs; Q1FY27 other income was lifted by provision reversals; the tax bill exceeds PBT.
AR FY26 note 27; Q1FY27 call; GAM
Guidance credibility: FY26 guidance was cut from low single-digit growth (May-2025) to flat (Oct-2025) and the year ended at -3% and a loss.
Executive pay rose 67-126% in a loss year (Chairperson 74x, CEO 73x the employee median).
AR FY26 managerial remuneration table; GAM
Carlyle's 17.95% stake is an overhang: two sell-down attempts were reported (Jul-2025, Aug-2026) and both were called off.
Leverage sits above CARE's 3.5x trigger; contingent Kenalog payments (up to US$65 mn) and Lexington capex keep net debt high through FY27.
gaps: Segment EBITDA: Piramal reports one segment and publishes no business-level EBITDA; our CDMO/CHG/PCH margins are GAM estimates anchored on JM Financial (CDMO high single digit) and CARE (PCH low single digit).
